findings.summary: The follow-up at 48d1df2 changes only the result record, the contract document and one line of the test's failure diagnostic. All eight runtime and UI files (git blobs) are byte-identical to 264a3d2: family-space 0f10b66, adult-http 7730b3a, the client 87bc50c, LoopFamilyHome 6542a50, the CSS b43517c, main.tsx b24b4af, LoopPreview c8a7a01 and LoopChildSetup e837e86. The eight-scenario native run on 264a3d2 therefore still applies; the follow-up adds only a fresh closed-access spot check, which it labels as such. The controller reran every check on this tree: 68/68 app tests, the build, all protected PG/HTTP/journal probes, 76 route identities and the seeded private scan. Review 1's findings are resolved. The REPORT and FAMILY_SPACE_CONTRACT now list the direct dependents 03-C, 04-A, 09-B and 09-C, plus the 04-B, 04-C and 08-A interface consumers, and claim none of them complete. The stale pending/preliminary wording is superseded by dated actual evidence. The test diagnostic regex now matches loop-family-space.test.mjs. The poll-during-open nit is openly left unfixed, as stated. The three card acceptance criteria remain met, as established in review 1. I also checked the code against the 00-B contracts (v1.1.1), lines 1–79 read in 40-line sections. The family projection matches them: one claim category per request (pending, reserved or consumed); capacity moves booked → completed or released; the due time is the original receipt plus 86,400 seconds and is never reset; ready means consumed, completed and assigned; payload IDs confer no authority; the consent lock is taken first; no-store is set. Saved-only rows book nothing and promise no deadline. Gates G-E03, G-E04 and G-E05, the offer, and the real-data, public and content gates all stay closed. DECISION-033 submission-time eligibility is shown as approved, not reopened. What I have read across this session: in full, AGENTS, SOURCE_OF_TRUTH, GOVERNANCE, APPROVALS, PRODUCT_V1 v0.4.1, the engineering README, ENGINEERING_DESIGN_V1, MODULE_GUIDE and REVIEW_NOTES, and PROJECT_CONTEXT v1.95 lines 1–1309, which review 1 read in large untruncated chunks rather than 40-line sections. Also the 03-A card, the protected probe, the play-service resume and reconcile code, the adult-http body guard, the TASKS.json dependents, the 00-C F04 row, and now 00-B lines 1–79. PRODUCT_DECISIONS.md and WORK_MODULES_V1.md are not in the pinned context directory, so I could not read them; I disclose that below.

findings.title: PRODUCT_DECISIONS and WORK_MODULES_V1 missing from pinned context
findings.problem: The follow-up asked for the product-decision and module rows that review 1 skipped. Neither approved/product-v1/PRODUCT_DECISIONS.md nor approved/product-v1/WORK_MODULES_V1.md is in the pinned directory .agent-loop/app-context/CODEX-03-A; a glob for them found nothing. I used TASKS.json (03-A scope and dependents) and the 00-B module-ownership table (WM-03/04/07/08) instead. Neither card criterion depends on an open decision row, and both PRODUCT_V1 and the 00-B contracts state the relevant open choices (G-E04 offer and allocation), so this does not block. It is missing evidence, though, not a review of those files.
findings.fix_check: Future pinned context for WM-03 cards includes both approved files, or the controller states explicitly that they are not required, so the reviewer can read the CODEX-WM-03 module row and the PD-D decision rows directly.

findings.title: A poll or focus during an open still discards it with no notice (left unfixed)
findings.problem: Carried over unchanged from review 1. refresh() increments openSequence, so a same-context poll or focus that lands while an open is in flight silently drops its result. No stale private data is shown, but the parent may need to tap Open again. The REPORT and the contract both record this as not fixed.
findings.fix_check: A later UI change either re-issues the open after the scope check or shows a retry status when a recheck invalidates an in-flight open.

findings.title: Status file result_commit points to the review-record commit, not 48d1df2
findings.problem: result_commit is f2f9ebb, the commit that recorded review 1. The final reviewed tree is 48d1df2. This file is controller-managed, but a stale pointer could pin acceptance to the wrong revision; review-notes item 8 records the same pattern for the architecture task.
findings.fix_check: Before the controller records acceptance, result_commit names 48d1df2 or the exact commit it merges.
